scenes.headline:
You know the book.
And it still lives in a cabinet
card: Knows the cover better than the system does
and still works out of a drawer
scenes.say: Somewhere right now there is someone who knows general insurance inside out, and still runs the book out of a filing cabinet.

scenes.headline: You retype it. You wait. / And the history is in a drawer
scenes.say: The proposal form retyped by hand. An endorsement waiting three days in somebody's inbox. Last year's file in a drawer, and the year before it in another.

scenes.headline: You would not be building one. / It is already there
scenes.line: Personal and commercial, fleets included. Every endorsement written to the Act — and we drive that ourselves.
scenes.say: You would not be building a book. There is one: seven lines, personal and commercial, renewals in all twelve months, and every endorsement on it written to the Act.

scenes.headline: Every term since the policy began

check: already on the screen when you open it

scenes.say: Before you open a file, every term since the policy began is on the screen. What was covered, at what value, what was paid, and the claims.

scenes.headline: Read for you, / and checked against our record

bill.out: The desk says so, before it reaches the client

scenes.say: The insurer's notice is read for you, and every figure checked against our own record. If the two disagree, the desk says so before it reaches the client.

scenes.headline: Nobody is left / waiting on somebody’s memory

phone.title: Your renewal
steps: at seven, if nobody has spoken to them
They sign in and read it
every year of their own cover
cues: Their own history, in their hands

scenes.say: And the client is never left waiting on somebody's memory. They are reminded at fourteen days, then ten. If nobody has spoken to them, a call opens itself at seven. They sign in, read every year of their own cover, confirm it and sign, on their phone.

scenes.headline: The part a system cannot do
cards: what the cover does, and what it does not
the Act and market conduct — we do not wait to be told
scenes.say: Which leaves you the part no system can do. Endorsements written properly. The renewal conversation. Telling a client plainly what the cover does and what it does not. We drive compliance here, and we do not wait to be told.

scenes.eyebrow: The part most people in this work never get
scenes.headline: A change is not a ticket. / It is a decision

script.rhead: Here · the rule, in the desk

scenes.say: And a change you ask for is not a ticket that goes somewhere else to wait. It is written into the desk, and runs on every file that week.

scenes.headline: The paperwork is finished. / The advice is not

r: not settled — and that is yours
split.line: How this agency looks after its clients is the part we want you for.

scenes.say: The paperwork is finished. The advice is not. That is the job.

scenes.urlsub:
Your CV and fifteen minutes.
Read by the Branch Manager alone.
scenes.say: Client manager, general insurance. If you are good at this and you have stopped learning, come and look after the book.
